title: Passwordless sudo grant is unbounded after one OS approval
reasoning: Enabling agent sudo access writes a sudoers rule that grants the current user `NOPASSWD: ALL`, which removes password prompts for every sudo command on the machine, not just WindieOS-controlled commands. A single successful pkexec approval therefore permanently broadens privilege for the whole user session/system until disabled, so any later local process running as that user can invoke arbitrary sudo commands without authentication.
reproduction: On Linux, enable passwordless sudo through this handler. After it returns success, run any unrelated `sudo` command from the same user account; it will no longer require a password because the sudoers rule applies to `ALL` commands.
recommendation: Replace the blanket sudoers rule with the narrowest command allowlist needed by WindieOS, or avoid persistent sudoers mutation and use per-operation OS authorization. If broad access is intentionally required, gate it behind explicit high-risk copy and add a verification path that reports the exact sudoers scope.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for the generated sudoers content or for limiting the privilege scope of the rule.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a unit test for the enable-script builder that asserts the sudoers rule does not contain `NOPASSWD: ALL` and only grants approved WindieOS command paths.
minimumFixScope: frontend/src/main/agent_sudo_access_handler.cjs and focused tests around generated sudoers rules and disable behavior.
